stem: Chirag must construct rectangle $ABCD$ so that diagonal $AC$ divides $\angle DAB$ into $60^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$. The diagram shows the right angle at $A$ and those parts along diagonal $AC$.

parts.text: Which plan locates the next sides and vertex $D$ correctly?

options.text: Use $\angle DAB=90^{\circ}$, so the $60^{\circ}$ part leaves $30^{\circ}$; then place sides and vertex $D$ from that split.
Call the finished figure diagonal $AC$ only.
Place vertex $D$ first, then force $\angle DAB$ to become $90^{\circ}$ from that placement.
Choose the plan only because $60$ is the largest printed angle number among $60$, $30$, and $90$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A rectangle corner is 90°, so a 60° part of the diagonal split leaves 30°, which locates the next sides and D.

teacher.key_rationale: 90° at A with a 60° part leaves 30° for placing sides and D. Naming only the diagonal substitutes a label. Placing D first then forcing 90° reverses the construction order. Picking the largest print is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle as rectangle with 60°/30° diagonal split at A.
